newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat warns Israel not to gamble with peace.
newsitem.headline: Arafat warns Israel not to gamble with peace.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat warned Israel on Saturday not to "gamble" with Middle East peace by expanding Jewish settlements in occupied Arab lands.
"The current Israeli government gambles with the peace process if settlement activity is increased," Arafat told reporters in self-ruled Jenin in the West Bank.
Arafat's warning shot comes on the eve of a new round of peace talks between Israel and the Palestinian Authority on implementation of outstanding issues in interim peace deals.

Eight joint committees were due to open talks on Sunday to deal with the fine points of a 1995 peace deal, including arrangements for Palestinian sea and air ports, a "safe passage" between the West Bank and Gaza, economic and civil affairs and "people to people" cooperation.
"We hope there will be quick accomplishments," Arafat said.
The sides agreed to the talks as part of a U.S.-brokered peace agreement in January that saw 80 percent of the West Bank town of Hebron handed over to Palestinian self-rule.
Arafat called on Israel to respect a March 7 deadline for the first of three planned Israeli withdrawals from West Bank rural areas slated to end by mid-1998.
"We hope that Israel will implement its promises."
Some 130,000 Jews are scattered amid more than two million Palestinians in settlements built in the West Bank and Gaza, occupied by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war.
Palestinians fear Israel will try and accelerate building in occupied areas in advance of the future pullbacks and "final status" peace talks, due to begin next month.

"We view with great alarm the Israeli steps that not only are a violation of the agreement but are a sign of ill-will and are preempting the outcome of the permanent status issues," Palestinian Higher Education Minister Hanan Ashrawi told reporters after a cabinet meeting on Friday.
Arafat said Palestinian prisoners still remaining in Israeli jails would be released "very soon...as what happened with the women prisoners."
Israel released 30 women prisoners earlier this week under a peace deal. Palestinian sources say some 3,000 prisoners remain imprisoned. Israeli sources put the figure closer to 2,200.
